recentItems.title: Ciaran Murphy & Stephen Thorne | On The Wire On The Road
recentItems.description:
On The Wire On The Road reaches its final episode, as Andrew Blair White spends a morning at two of the most promising young yards in Ireland.

First to Charlestown Stud and Ciaran Murphy, who came to racing from a GAA family with no horses in it and now trains across both codes off eighty boxes.

Then on to Stephen Thorne, who won the all-weather trainers' championship in his first season with a licence and is focusing around twenty horses rather than fifty.

recentItems.title: 1/33F Najidi Storm Beaten in British Racing's Biggest Shock | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Najidi Storm became the shortest-priced loser in the history of British racing when he was beaten into second in the Cleansing Service Group Novice Stakes at Goodwood at odds of 1-33.

Charlie Pike’s aptly-named Wreck It Ronnie, beaten a combined 22 and a half lengths in his only two previous outings, made virtually all in the hands of Kieren Fox and Lewis Edmunds could not reel him in on the Harry Charlton-trained favourite, who is a brother to 2019 St Leger hero Logician.

The only other runner in the 10-furlong contest, Dream Of Albion, was a well tailed off 76 lengths in arrears. The previous record was jointly held by Doom (2023) and Royal Forest (1948), who were both beaten at 1-25.

Brian O’Keeffe of BOYLE Sports, said: “We’ve witnessed the shortest-priced loser in British racing history, but that doesn’t mean it was a good result for the layers.

“Najidi Storm might have been an ‘acca’ buster for a number of punters, but when one is put in that short, they’re often keen to look elsewhere.

“This time, their eye was drawn to the winner, Wreck It Ronnie, who was unfortunately the biggest liability in the race in our book.”

Paddy Power spokesman Paul Binfield said: “Wreck It Ronnie sure lived up to his name with favourite-backers and the winner was actually a loser in the book with punters taking a chance against the very short-priced ‘jolly’.”

recentItems.title: Behind The Scenes At The Arqana Yearling Sale | The Bloodstock Files
recentItems.description:
The Bloodstock Files goes to Deauville for the Arqana August Yearling Sale, the first of the European season — and hands the episode to Emma Berry and Bernard Condren in their day jobs as journalist and auctioneer.

Bernard walks his lots in the morning, explaining what he looks for in a yearling, why the walk matters, and how twenty-six years of auctioneering started with bit-spotting at Goffs while he should have been at school. Then, wearing camera glasses on the rostrum, he sells a Justify colt for €1.25 million with Godolphin and Coolmore going toe to toe, and follows it with a Wootton Bassett colt at €800,000.

Emma is out with the TDN team, and talks to Henri Bozo, director at Ecurie des Monceaux. Plus Pierre Boulard, Willie Mullins's man in France, on why they're now buying flat yearlings with enough stamina and scope to jump if the flat doesn't work out.

recentItems.title: The Verdict: Sprint Cup Analysis | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Angus McNae and Josh Kerr go through the week's action with the RaceIQ sectional data, headed by Almeraq's win in the Betfair Sprint Cup.

Almeraq is the World Pool Race of the Week, beating Paborus with last year's winner Big Mojo third — though the clock has a view on how the race was run, with a time index of 3.1 against a meeting average of 4.9 and a winning time nearly two seconds above par.

Also from Haydock on Saturday, First Law broke fastest of all and quickened through three very fast furlongs to win the Ascendant Stakes from Rocket Boy, and Aegean Prince was cruising three out before landing the Old Borough Cup.

Plus the fastest performances of the week away from the Group 1 — Pride Of Arras posting the best time index of the lot at Kempton on Saturday, Fortitudine going quicker than par over a mile and three at Kempton on Wednesday, and Sharaad at Haydock on Thursday, who switched leads inside the final furlong and took some pulling up.

recentItems.title: Joseph O'Brien: My Team For The Irish Champions Festival 2026 | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Joseph O'Brien talks Donn McClean through his team for the Irish Champions Festival with Leopardstown on the Saturday and the Curragh on the Sunday.

Thundering On, his Epsom Oaks winner, has had a mid-season break and takes her chance in the Blandford Stakes, with rain forecast that shouldn't harm her. James J Braddock, third in the Epsom Derby, has been gelded since and returns in the Kilternan Stakes with international targets in mind later in the year.

Plus a look back at a season that has already brought more winners than the last two, and why the weekend matters as much as it does.
